prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a few quick questions so I can give a targeted recommendation:
- How badly were you injured (minor, moderate, severe/hospitalized)?
- Was the accident in Pleasanton on public roads? Was it a multi‑vehicle crash, a hit‑and‑run, or something else (e.g., a commercial vehicle, rideshare, bike/pedestrian)?
- Have you already spoken to an insurance adjuster or signed anything?
- Do you want a lawyer who tries cases in court or one who focuses on negotiating settlements?

If you just want general guidance right away, here’s how to pick the best lawyer for your case and what to do next.

1) Urgent steps you should take now (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical care and keep records.
- Preserve evidence: photos of injuries/vehicles/scenes, repair estimates, police report number, witness contacts.
- Don’t give recorded statements or sign releases for the other party’s insurer without a lawyer.
- Note: California’s statute of limitations for most personal injury claims is 2 years from the injury (shorter if a government entity is involved). Act promptly.

2) What kind of lawyer you should look for
- Specialization: personal injury attorney (car accidents, wrongful death, pedestrian/bicycle).
- Local experience: someone who handles Alameda County/Pleasanton cases and knows local courts and insurance practices.
- Trial experience: if your injuries are serious or liability is contested, pick a lawyer who will take cases to trial if needed.
- Track record: settlements and verdicts, client testimonials, AV ratings or peer reviews.

3) Practical search options (local resources)
- Alameda County Bar Association lawyer referral service.
- State Bar of California website to confirm license and any disciplinary history.
- Consumer sites (Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell) for ratings and reviews.
- Ask friends/family or your treating medical providers for referrals.

4) Questions to ask at an initial (usually free) consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident cases? How many like mine?
- What percentage of your cases settle vs go to trial?
- What is your fee (contingency %)? Any other costs I might owe?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?
- Estimated timeline and likely outcomes for my case.
- Can you provide references from recent clients?

5) Typical fees and costs
- Most personal injury lawyers charge a contingency fee (commonly 33%–40% if the case goes to trial). Confirm whether the percentage changes if the case settles before or after suit is filed.
- You may be responsible for out‑of‑pocket costs (filing fees, expert fees) which are usually advanced by the firm and reimbursed from recovery.

6) Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific recovery amount.
- High-pressure “sign now” tactics.
- Reluctance to put fee agreement in writing.
- Poor communication or evasive answers about experience.

7) If you want, I can:
- Search for well‑reviewed personal injury attorneys in Pleasanton / Alameda County and give you a short list (3–5) with contact info and why they might fit your case.
- Draft questions or a checklist you can bring to consultations.
Tell me whether you’d like local referrals and answer the short questions at the top so I can tailor the suggestions.
